span: a dying declaration, if it is free of tutoring, prompting, etc. can form the sole basis of conviction
why: Court states the principle as established, then finds the declarations insufficient on the facts; the principle itself is affirmed, not rejected.

span: Dying declaration can be the sole basis of the conviction if it inspires the full confidence of the court
why: Headnote holding that a dying declaration that inspires full confidence can alone support conviction; headnote confidence is capped.

span: the Court can convict the accused only on the basis of a dying declaration
why: Court states that where a dying declaration is truthful, voluntary and untainted, conviction can rest on it alone, before finding doubts on the facts.

span: If the court is satisﬁ ed that the dying declaration is true and voluntary it can base conviction on it, without corroboration.
why: Quotes the Paniben principles from Vikas; the current court's own adoption is not shown in this passage.

span: It is unsafe to record the conviction on the basis of a dying declaration alone in the cases where suspicion
why: Headnote says a dying declaration alone is unsafe where suspicion about its correctness arises, while noting its sanctity otherwise; it does not deny that a reliable one can suffice. Headnote confidence is capped.

span: Dying declaration cannot form the sole basis for conviction unless it is corroborated
why: Headnote text states that corroboration is needed, yet adds that courts rely on it if it inspires confidence and the earlier headnote says it can be the sole basis; the headnote is internally mixed. Headnote confidence is capped.

span: If the dying declaration suffers from some infirmity, it cannot alone form the basis of conviction.
why: Summary of earlier decisions that both limits and permits reliance on a dying declaration alone (reliable ones can be relied on without corroboration); adoption by the current court is not shown.

span: it is upon the duty of the court to see the extent to which the dying declaration is entitled to credit
why: Court discusses admissibility and the duty to test credibility, without stating whether it can alone convict.

span: it cannot be laid down as an absolute rule of law that a dying declaration cannot form the sole basis of conviction unless it is corroborated
why: Quotes the Khushal Rao yardstick; adoption by the current court is not shown in this passage.

span: can be the sole basis for conviction without any corroboration
why: Headnote holding that an authentic dying declaration can alone support conviction after the court is satisfied of voluntariness and credibility; headnote confidence is capped.
